[Management API](admin-api.html)

What this realm's OID4VP Verifier asks a wallet for.

Every answer is checked against the model shown here before it is sent, and no answer carries a member its model does not list. A member shown as *any JSON* is one whose shape belongs to somebody else, and says whose. `.{key}` is a key that is data, and `[]` an element of a list.

## GET /admin-api/verifications

`getVerifications`

**A verification's outcome, or the verifications still open**

With `state`: what the Verifier decided, with `found: true`: `state`, `nonce`, `client_id`, `requested`, `dcql_query`, `received` (whether a wallet has answered) and `verdict` (`ok`, `checks`, `claims`, `disclosed`, …, and `presentationDigest`, the SHA-256 of the presentation, which is never kept itself; null until it answers). A state this realm holds no record of is 404 with `found: false` (STS-VC-0042).

Without `state`: the realm's open verifications, newest first — at most `limit` of `total` — each its `state`, what was asked (`format`, `responseType`, `responseMode`, `byReference`, `clientId`, `requested`), `expiresAt`, and what was decided (`received`, `ok`, `decidedAt`, the disclosed claim NAMES, `failedChecks`, a wallet's `error`). A wallet SIGN-IN is not listed: it is a person signing in, not a verification an administrator asked for. The Verifier request tab draws this list.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/vc` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| `state` | query | string |  | The `state` `POST /verifications/start` answered. |

## POST /admin-api/verifications/start

`startVerification`

**Start an OpenID4VP verification: build a request for a wallet**

Builds a presentation request — the one door a verification starts at since #594 — and answers how a wallet is handed it: `walletUrl` (what a same-device start redirects to: the web wallet `wallet` named or `oid4vp.walletUrl` configures, with the request on its query, or — with neither, the default — the same as `requestUri`), `requestUri` (the request under the scheme a wallet app registers for: `openid4vp://`, HAIP's `haip-vp://` where `oid4vp.walletInvocation` says so, or SIOPv2's `siopv2://` for an ID Token alone; what a cross-device QR code carries), `wallet` (the address or scheme before the query), `query` itself, and — by reference — the `request_uri` the wallet fetches the signed Request Object from. `state` names it; `GET /verifications?state=` reads its outcome.

The body names what the page's query names, every member optional: `format` (a format id, `GET /verifier-request` lists them; the configured default when absent), `by` (`value` or `reference`), `client_id_prefix` (a signed request's Client Identifier Prefix — naming one asks for a request by reference), `response_type`, `response_mode`, `mode` (`same-device` or `cross-device`, which only says which of the two addresses a caller means to use) and `wallet` (held to `oid4vp.walletUrl` and `oid4vp.allowedWalletUrls` wherever only registered addresses are accepted).

`redirect_uri` (#594) is the caller's own page the Response Endpoint sends the wallet to once it has answered (OpenID4VP 1.0 section 8.2). Wherever only registered addresses are accepted it must be one of the CALLING CLIENT's registered redirect URIs, matched whole (400, STS-VC-0123); left off, the Response Endpoint answers no `redirect_uri` — what a wallet on another device wants.

What the request ASKS FOR is the Verifier request's configuration (`/verifier-request`), frozen onto the transaction now. Refused as the page refuses: 400 for what the request names wrongly (STS-VC-0032) and for a wallet this realm will not send a request to (STS-VC-0033), and 500 with the builder's own code where no request can be built — a Verifier Attestation this realm cannot use (STS-VC-0092), an x509 Client Identifier with nothing to certify (STS-VC-0110 to STS-VC-0113). Answered in every mode: this is an administrator asking.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/vc#vc-tab-verifier-request` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body** (optional)

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `by` | one of `value`, `reference` |  |  |
| `client_id_prefix` | one of `pre-registered`, `decentralized_identifier`, `verifier_attestation`, `openid_federation`, `x509_san_dns`, `x509_hash` |  |  |
| `format` | string |  | A format id: dc+sd-jwt, jwt_vc_json, ldp_vc, mso_mdoc. Not a closed set here, as on `/verifier-request/format`: a form-encoded `+` arrives as a space and is put back, and the Verifier refuses anything else by name. |
| `mode` | one of `same-device`, `cross-device` |  |  |
| `redirect_uri` | string |  | The caller's page the wallet is sent to once the Verifier has answered (#594); a registered redirect URI of the calling client wherever only registered addresses are accepted. |
| `response_mode` | one of `direct_post`, `direct_post.jwt`, `form_post` |  |  |
| `response_type` | one of `vp_token`, `id_token`, `vp_token id_token` |  |  |
| `wallet` | string |  | A web wallet to send the holder to, if not `oid4vp.walletUrl` or a wallet app (the default). |

**200**: `state`, `walletUrl`, `requestUri`, `query`, the `request_uri` by reference, and what was asked: `ok`, `message`, `state`, `nonce`, `mode`, `format`, `responseType`, `responseMode`, `byReference`, `clientId`, `requested`, `dcql_query`, `expiresAt`, `wallet`, `walletUrl`, `requestUri`, `query`, `redirectUri` ('' for none) and, by reference, `request_uri`.

## GET /admin-api/verifier-request

`getVerifierRequest`

**What this realm's OID4VP Verifier asks a wallet for**

The claims, the credential format, and the `dcql_query` they build — from the function that builds the real one, so this is the next Authorization Request rather than a description of it.

Each catalogue row also says whether the ISSUER currently mints that claim. The two settings are deliberately separate and their disagreeing is a state to report rather than one to prevent: a Verifier asking for a claim nothing here issues is the only way to exercise what a wallet does with a request it cannot satisfy.

`recentVerifications` (#587) is `GET /verifications` without a `state` — the open verifications and their outcomes the tab lists under its Start a verification form.

**Mirrors** `GET /admin/vc` on the admin console.

The reply also carries `protocolEndpoints`: every endpoint of this family in the realm the call arrived in, as `{ name, methods, url }` (plus `route` for an HTTP endpoint, `transport` for a socket, and `registered: false` for a route the router no longer has).

Scope: `admin:read`.

## POST /admin-api/verifier-request/add

`addRequestedClaim`

**Ask for one more claim**

A claim NOT in the catalogue is accepted, and is the point rather than a loose end: nothing here issues it, so it is the only way to exercise what a wallet does with a request it cannot satisfy. The reply says so, and the Verifier will then refuse the presentation on the "Requested claims" check and name it.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/vc#vc-tab-verifier-request` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

## POST /admin-api/verifier-request/format

`setRequestFormat`

**Set the credential format a request asks in**

Applies to a request that does not name a format itself; the three format links on the Verifier page name one explicitly and are unaffected.

The DCQL PATH DIFFERS BY FORMAT and the reply shows it: top level for dc+sd-jwt, under credentialSubject for jwt_vc_json, and under the vendored JSON-LD context's own term for ldp_vc — which cannot carry every claim at all.

## POST /admin-api/verifier-request/select

`selectRequestedClaims`

**Set the whole list of requested claims**

Reaches the wire as the `claims` member of the next Authorization Request's dcql_query.

An EMPTY array is a legitimate call and not an empty form: DCQL reads an absent `claims` member as the WHOLE credential, so requesting nothing asks the wallet for everything — the opposite of what selective disclosure is for, which is exactly why being able to ask for it matters.

The claims a request asks for are FROZEN onto the transaction when it is built, so a change here never re-judges a presentation already in flight.

**Mirrors** `POST /admin/vc#vc-tab-verifier-request` on the admin console.

Scope: `admin:write`.

**Request body**

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `claims` | list | yes | Top-level claim names. A credential carries one Disclosure per top-level claim, so `address` is one unit however many attributes feed it. |
| `claims[]` | string |  |  |

**200**: What is requested now, and what changed.

| Member | Type | Required | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `added` | list |  |  |
| `added[]` | string |  |  |
